policy.promotion_rule: Implementation alone never proves edge. A trading component may be presented as validated only when its evidence record names the test type, date range, sample size, costs, result file, and acceptance decision.
policy.performance_rule: Historical, replay, paper, funded-evaluation, and live results must remain separate. No blended performance claims.

items.name: Primary market: MES / ES
items.claim: The project is designed around MES/ES rather than a multi-market strategy.
items.note: Verified as an accepted project constraint, not as proof that MES/ES is more profitable than another market.

items.name: Reference ORB: 08:00–08:15 New York
items.claim: The current project direction uses the 08:00–08:15 New York range as a reference level.
items.note: Accepted current reference window. Its standalone edge versus 09:30 variants remains unproven and must be tested separately.

items.name: Primary new-entry window: 09:30–10:30 New York
items.claim: The primary operating model stops initiating new trades after 10:30 New York time.
items.note: Accepted risk constraint. The exact cutoff still requires isolated performance attribution.

items.name: Force flat by 11:00 New York
items.claim: The primary model closes remaining exposure by 11:00 New York time.
items.note: Accepted operating rule, not yet isolated as an edge contributor.

items.name: Maximum one planned trade per day
items.claim: The primary model permits one planned trade per day.
items.note: Accepted operating rule. A second-trade model remains a separate experiment.

items.name: ORB breakout → retest → continuation
items.claim: The current Pine files implement a breakout-retest continuation state machine.

items.name: Liquidity sweep → reclaim/rejection → continuation
items.claim: This is the preferred research direction for translating Mason's discretionary process into mechanical logic.
items.note: Preferred hypothesis, not validated production logic.

items.name: VWAP directional alignment
items.claim: Long signals require price above VWAP and short signals require price below VWAP when enabled.
items.note: The repository contains claims that VWAP adds edge, but no accepted isolated attribution record has been located.

items.name: EMA directional alignment
items.claim: EMA alignment exists as an optional code toggle.
items.note: Implementation is not validation. Keep out of the active Trade Bible until isolated testing is accepted.

items.name: 35% ORB-body or 0.75× ATR displacement gate
items.claim: The current Pine implementation accepts either threshold as displacement confirmation.
items.note: The thresholds require head-to-head sensitivity testing and out-of-sample confirmation.

items.name: ORB range gate: 5–50 points
items.claim: The current Pine files reject ORB ranges outside the configured minimum and maximum.
items.note: These defaults must be validated for instrument, contract, data feed, and volatility regime.

items.name: ORB midpoint retest
items.claim: Midpoint is the current default retest selection in the v1.1 Pine implementation.
items.note: Default input does not establish superiority.

items.name: Red-news proximity block
items.claim: A news filter is requested in the research design but no production implementation and accepted test record are present.

items.name: FVG as a required confluence
items.claim: FVG appears as a candidate setup variable, not an accepted mandatory rule.

items.name: Second trade after a first loss
items.claim: A second-trade model may be researched only as a separate configuration with a hard daily stop.

items.name: Blind ORB breakout entry
items.claim: An ORB break alone is not sufficient authorization to enter.

items.name: Rank candidates by net profit alone
items.claim: Candidate ranking must prioritize survival, drawdown, consistency, and validation quality before total profit.
